findings.issue_text: packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:96` — `await prisma.credential.update({` but `prisma` is never imported (imports end line 20; only occurrence in file). TS2304 at build; at runtime `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined` in `getClient()`, called from the constructor → **every Salesforce booking/availability path is dead**, not just credential-sync users.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97` — `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` … `data: { key },`. The helper returns the zod **safeParse wrapper** (`return refreshTokenResponse;`, parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:29), not `.data`. `Credential.key` is overwritten with `{"success":true,"data":{…}}`; next load `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` (line 75) throws → Google Calendar permanently bricked after the first refresh. The other two call sites (office365calendar:264, salesforce:92) unwrap `.data`, proving this one is wrong. `let refreshTokenResponse;` (`any`) suppressed the type error.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8` — `[z.string().toString()]: z.number(),` / `[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional(),`. Both computed keys stringify to the literal `"[object Object]"`; the second overwrites the first. `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is really `{access_token: string, "[object Object]"?: unknown}`, and `z.object` strips the rest → in sync mode `expiry_date`/`expires_in`/`scope`/`instance_url`/`refresh_token` are all silently dropped before persistence. The docstring ("Assume that any property with a number is the expiry / Allow other properties") describes behavior zod cannot do without `.catchall()`/`z.record()`.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25` — `if (!refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token) { refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"; }` sits **outside** the sharing-mode branch. office365calendar:264 spreads it into `o365AuthCredentials` and writes it at line 270 → a real Microsoft refresh token is replaced in the DB by the literal string `"refresh_token"`. Next refresh POSTs `refresh_token=refresh_token` → `invalid_grant`, unrecoverable without re-consent. Hits self-hosters who never enabled the feature.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:25` (conf 50, P0) — `req.headers[...] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. If `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is unset and the caller omits the header, both sides are `undefined` and the guard passes; the handler then writes `key: keys` for any attacker-supplied `reqBody.userId` with no ownership check → unauthenticated takeover of any user's Google/Stripe/Salesforce connection. Only `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` stands in the way; the route asserts no local non-empty-secret invariant.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:59` — `await throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam({ teamId: state?.teamId ?? null, userId });` is placed **after** the `if (state?.teamId) { … return; }` block (30–56), so it only ever runs with `teamId: null`. The branch that actually creates a team-wide credential is gated only on `members: { some: { userId, accepted: true } }` — any accepted member can plant a team-scoped Stripe/Salesforce/HubSpot credential bound to their own external account. Upstream cal.com calls this guard *before* the branch.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3,15` — `refreshFunction: () => any` and `return response;` (raw `Response`) in sync mode vs the app SDK's object otherwise; `any` collapses the union so TS checks nothing. googlecalendar:94 `const token = res?.data;` → `undefined` → `token.access_token` TypeError, swallowed by the `catch` at 103 (only special-cases `"invalid_grant"`) → refresh silently never works. hubspot:177 `const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)` is a type lie.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:5` vs `parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:15` — the mode predicate is duplicated and the copies disagree (`&& userId` present in one, absent in the other). For **team** credentials (`userId === null`) the token is fetched from the real provider (full response) but parsed with the minimum schema → stripped to `{access_token, refresh_token: "refresh_token"}`. Enabling sync destroys every team-owned credential on its next refresh.

packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:192,198` — `hubspotRefreshToken.expiryDate = Math.round(Date.now() + hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn * 1000);` then `key: hubspotRefreshToken as any`. In sync mode this is a `Response`: `expiresIn` undefined → `NaN`, and a `Response` serializes to `{}` → credential key destroyed. `catch (e) { this.log.error(e); }` (line 203) swallows it; `getToken()` resolves `undefined`.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75` — an unconditional `fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token")` **plus** a DB write added to `getClient()`, which runs from the constructor on every booking create/update/delete and availability computation. No `isExpired` check (every other app has one) → Salesforce OAuth rate limits + unbounded write amplification + concurrent read-modify-write on the row with no version/`FOR UPDATE`.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:106` — after persisting the refreshed token, the connection is still built from the stale line-73 capture: `accessToken: credentialKey.access_token, instanceUrl: credentialKey.instance_url`. The refresh is pure cost; requests keep using the expired token → `INVALID_SESSION_ID`.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:98` — `data: { key: { ...accessTokenParsed.data, refresh_token: credentialKey.refresh_token } }` replaces the whole key; `instance_url`, `id`, `signature` are dropped (all but `access_token` in sync mode) → next `getClient` reads `instanceUrl: undefined`. Also discards any rotated refresh token Salesforce returns.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:50` — `appStoreMetadata[app.slug as keyof typeof appStoreMetadata]`, but `appStoreMetadata` is keyed by **dirName**. For exactly the apps this feature wires up (`google-calendar`/`googlecalendar`, `office365-calendar`/`office365calendar`, `lark-calendar`/`larkcalendar`, `msteams`/`office365video`) the lookup is `undefined` → the webhook always 404s. The `as keyof typeof` cast suppressed the error; cal.com ships `getAppFromSlug()` for this.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62` — `findFirst({ where: { userId, appId } })` with no `orderBy` and no backing unique constraint (the comment "Can't use prisma upsert as we don't know the id" admits it), while `createOAuthAppCredential` always `create`s. Users legitimately hold N credentials per app (two Google accounts) → an arbitrary heap-order row is overwritten with the other account's tokens; concurrent deliveries both see no row and both `create` (TOCTOU).

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:78` — `key: keys` written with zero per-app validation (`keys: z.string()` is the only schema). Each app owns a credential schema (`googleCredentialSchema`, `webexTokenSchema`, `O365AuthCredentials`); none is applied. Full replacement, no backup → a payload missing `refresh_token`/`instance_url` destroys those fields, surfacing much later as a zod throw inside a booking flow. HTTP 200 either way.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:57` — `symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || "")` plus `JSON.parse`, both unguarded: unset key → invalid AES key length → raw crypto 500 with no "encryption key not configured" signal.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:73` — the update sets `data: { key: keys }` and never clears `invalid`, which googlecalendar:112-116 sets on `invalid_grant`. A resynced credential stays filtered out as dead despite a 200 `Credentials updated for userId: …`.

packages/app-store/office365video/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:93` — `key: responseBody as unknown as Prisma.InputJsonValue` replaces the whole key, while `refreshOAuthTokens.ts:7` documents "The response should only contain the access token and expiry date" → `refresh_token` deleted; `expiry_date = Date.now()` (immediately expired) when `expires_in` is absent. Same clobber at `larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:98-105`. webex/office365calendar merge instead — the persistence strategy is inconsistent across the new abstraction.

packages/app-store/webex/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:88`, `hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177`, `larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:84`, `office365video/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:84` — the two halves of the feature landed on disjoint app sets: `refreshOAuthTokens` wired into 6 apps, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` into only 3. webex still hard-validates with `webexRefreshedTokenSchema.safeParse` (requires `refresh_token`, `refresh_token_expires_in`, literal `scope`/`token_type`), lark still unwraps `data.data.*` via `handleLarkError`, office365video still `handleErrorsJson<ITokenResponse>` → refresh deterministically fails or NaN-expires for 4 of the 6 apps the change claims to enable.

docs/tasks/task-001.md:2` — 31 files touching credential storage across 8 OAuth apps, **zero tests, fixtures, or manual repro steps**. The two modes are mutually exclusive at runtime, so the sync path demonstrably never executed — consistent with the unimported `prisma`, the `"[object Object]"` keys, and the four apps passing a `Response` into object-shaped code.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:3` (conf 50) — `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` imported from `@calcom/lib/constants` in three new files, but `packages/lib/constants.ts` is not in the diff and the feature's env vars are introduced fresh here. If the export doesn't already exist → TS2305 in all three. Confirm against the full tree (this snapshot is sparse).

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/decodeOAuthState.ts:9` — `const state: IntegrationOAuthCallbackState = JSON.parse(req.query.state);` — `state` is an unsigned, unvalidated, attacker-forgeable blob, not a CSRF nonce: (a) OAuth account-linking CSRF attaches the attacker's external account to a victim's credential; (b) `state.teamId` is the sole input to the ownership decision at createOAuthAppCredential.ts:30; (c) malformed `state` throws an unhandled `SyntaxError` → 500 mid-OAuth across all 8 callbacks. The type annotation enforces nothing at runtime.

packages/app-store/stripepayment/api/callback.ts:51` — `res.redirect(returnTo || getInstalledAppPath(...))` with `returnTo = JSON.parse(\`${req.query.state}\`).returnTo` and no `getSafeRedirectUrl` — the only callback in the diff missing it → open redirect at the highest-trust moment of a payments flow.

packages/app-store/larkcalendar/api/callback.ts:98` — `res.redirect(state?.returnTo ?? "/apps/installed");` in the catch path bypasses the `getSafeRedirectUrl` used on the success path (line 93) → open redirect on any throw inside the try.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24` — webhook secret compared with short-circuiting `!==`, no rate limit, no lockout, and the 403 body distinguishes "sharing disabled" from "invalid secret" → remote timing oracle for byte-by-byte secret recovery. Needs `crypto.timingSafeEqual` over length-checked buffers.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:57` (conf 50) — `|| ""` default-empty encryption key is a default-secret pattern; upstream `symmetricDecrypt` is AES-256-CBC with no MAC, so this credential-transport channel has no integrity protection and the 200-vs-500 divergence is a padding oracle. (Conf capped: `packages/lib/crypto.ts` absent from this tree.)

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:31` — `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` unguarded and no `req.method` check → any GET with the right header throws `ZodError` out of the handler → 500 + unhandled rejection instead of 405/400.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8` — the outbound sync POST carries **no** authentication (`body: new URLSearchParams({ calcomUserId, appSlug })`), no `response.ok` check, no scheme validation, while the inbound webhook does require a secret. Anything that can reach the endpoint can harvest any user's live access token by POSTing a user id.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8` — no `AbortSignal`/timeout, no retry, no circuit breaker, no error path; the provider fallback is unreachable once the flag is on. A hanging sync endpoint blocks every booking/availability/calendar write for all tenants; a 500 HTML body flows into each app's `handleErrorsJson` as an opaque integration failure.

packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:263-264` — deleted verbatim: `console.error("Outlook error grabbing new tokens ~ zodError:", tokenResponse.error, "MS response:", responseJson);`. Behavior changed from "log the zod error, keep old creds, continue" to `throw new Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")` with the offending payload discarded. The surviving `tokenResponse.success &&` guard is now dead code (same at salesforce:92-94).

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:86` — `if (response.statusText !== "OK")` discriminates on the optional HTTP/1.1 reason phrase, which is `""` over HTTP/2 → spurious 400 on a valid 200; use `response.ok`/`response.status`.

packages/app-store/webex/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:151` (conf 50, pre-existing) — `console.log("result of accessToken in fetchWebexApi", accessToken);` emits a live bearer token to logs on every meeting operation. The diff removed the analogous token-bearing log in office365calendar and should have removed this one in the file it rewrites.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:45` — `throw new Error("User does not belong to the team")` where the sibling failure uses `HttpError({ statusCode: 401 })` → an authz failure surfaces as a 500 to the OAuth callback.

.env.example:240` — `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT=""` has no comment at all; the only description of the contract lives in a code comment. Nothing documents that the POST body is form-encoded `calcomUserId`/`appSlug`, that the response must be JSON with `access_token` + expiry, or how to AES-encrypt `keys` → a self-hoster cannot implement the counterpart endpoint from this change.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:5` — team credentials (`userId === null`) silently fall through to `refreshFunction()`, which needs the local app secret a credential-sharing self-hoster deliberately doesn't have → team installs fail at refresh time rather than being rejected at install time.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/encodeOAuthState.ts:7` — `if (typeof req.query.state !== "string") return undefined;` → `state: undefined` in the auth URL, so a team install silently degrades to a personal install with a 200 and no log.

packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/api/add.ts:17` — `const redirectUri = WEBAPP_URL + \`/api/integrations/zoho-bigin/callback\`;` de-parameterized from `${appConfig.slug}` while lines 12 and 22 still use `appConfig.slug`/`appConfig.scope`. Two sources of truth in one handler; a `config.json` slug rename now yields a Zoho `redirect_uri_mismatch`. Unrelated to credential sync — the only non-import change in the zoho-bigin/stripepayment/tandemvideo group.

.env.example:242` — `# must be 32 bytes for AES256` immediately followed by `openssl rand -base64 24`. Contradictory: a reader following "32 bytes" literally (as directed 6 lines above) produces a 44-char key and gets an unexplained 500 at `symmetricDecrypt`.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/encodeOAuthState.ts:9` — a JSON identity round-trip duplicating `decodeOAuthState` line-for-line, with no shared type or codec. The `encode`/`decode` naming implies a transformation and validation boundary that don't exist.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:42` — `select: { id: true, members: { select: { userId: true } } }` loads a team's entire membership list on every OAuth install; `team` is only used for the truthiness check at line 45.

docs/tasks/task-001.md:1` — the intent anchor was authored ~11h *after* the code landed (commit 0633864 "task" vs b263064 "pr"), is the only file in that commit, and contains zero acceptance criteria → nothing records a human-accepted objective against which the credential-key format change, the removed O365 diagnostics, or the Zoho redirect change could be validated as intended.
NO FINDINGS — no test code exists in this diff, so this lens had nothing in scope (missing-verification is reported by Completeness above).

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8` — `[z.string().toString()]: z.number(),` / `[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional(),`. Both computed keys stringify to the literal `"[object Object]"`; the second overwrites the first. `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is really `{access_token: string, "[object Object]"?: unknown}`, and `z.object` strips the rest → in sync mode `expiry_date`/`expires_in`/`scope`/`instance_url`/`refresh_token` are all silently dropped before persistence. The docstring ("Assume that any property with a number is the expiry / Allow other properties") describes behavior zod cannot do without `.catchall()`/`z.record()`.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `minimumTokenResponseSchema` with computed property keys: `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional()`. In JavaScript, computed object keys are evaluated immediately to a single string; `z.string()` returns an object, so `.toString()` yields a fixed string key (at best a constant like "[object Object]" or similar), not “any string key”. The second computed key also resolves to a constant and will overwrite the first if identical. Therefore this schema does not implement “any numeric property” / “allow other properties”; instead it only defines `access_token` plus one constant-named key. Since `z.object(...)` defaults to stripping unknown keys, other fields like `expiry_date`/`expires_in` etc. would be dropped in sync mode, contradicting the comments and intended behavior. This is a concrete defect in the added code.

The specific claim that users can legitimately have multiple credentials per app isn't directly proven by this diff, but the nondeterminism and race/duplication risk are real defects introduced by the shown logic.
